scenes.title: 1964/1965 Córdoba Sunlit Arena: José Delgado Clicking a Handheld Radio Transmitter as an Articulated Porcelain Bull Sculpture Skids & Turns Sideways
scenes.era: 1965, La Alamiriya Ranch arena, Córdoba, Spain

layout.description: Sunlit circular Spanish sand arena framed by whitewashed stone walls under bright Andalusian daylight: at center stands José Delgado holding a compact brushed-aluminum handheld FM radio transmitter box with whip antenna, while three yards in front of him a life-scale **articulated matte-white porcelain bull sculpture** skids in a clean arc of golden sand, turning its head and shoulders sharply sideways off the charge line.

positions.who: José Delgado (mannequin in 1965 open-collar white shirt, dark trousers, and espadrilles)
positions.where: standing calm and upright in the sunlit sand pressing the toggle button on his handheld radio transmitter box
front hooves planted in a braking skid, head and torso pivoting smoothly 90 degrees sideways away from Delgado in response to the unilateral caudate motor-turn signal
positions.facing: three yards ahead on the sand arc

props.name: 1965 brushed-aluminum handheld FM radio transmitter with whip antenna
props.period_detail: wireless remote switch replacing tangled 1950s laboratory cables

props.name: life-scale articulated matte-white porcelain bull sculpture with tiny crown stimoceiver cap
props.period_detail: stages the charging-halt-and-turn trajectory cleanly under R46 porcelain animal aesthetics
props.physical_behavior: shows the physical sideways turn clearly

props.name: chalked sand trajectory arc ('Forward Charge -> Caudate Motor Turn')
props.period_detail: curved sand skid marks revealing a forced lateral motor veer rather than sleepy docility
props.physical_behavior: plants the visual clue to the scientific twist

actions.verb_sequence: barrels forward along the straight sand line -> Delgado clicks the handheld radio transmitter button -> bull's front hooves brake and its head/shoulders pivot briskly sideways off course

reactions.reaction: lowers the radio transmitter calmly as observers along the wooden barrier gasp
photograph the moment that landed on Page 1 of The New York Times

scenes.wardrobe: 1965 Spanish summer attire: crisp rolled-sleeve white cotton shirt, dark tailored trousers.
scenes.lighting: Crisp high-key Andalusian sunlight over pale golden sand and whitewashed walls.
scenes.recognition_hook: No sword, no tether wires — one click on a handheld radio box makes a charging bull skid and veer sideways three yards from his chest.

key_visual.description: a sunlit Spanish sand ring where a researcher in a white shirt presses a handheld radio transmitter with an antenna as an articulated matte-white porcelain bull sculpture brakes and turns sideways

scenes.title: Page 1 Hype vs Caudate Motor-Turn Reality (Valenstein & Horgan)

layout.description: Bright oak seminar table comparing the 1965 front-page headline placard beside a basal-ganglia caudate diagram and 16mm film frame analyzer.

positions.where: pointing to the unilateral caudate electrode site and curved turning path on the frame-by-frame diagram

props.name: Headline ('Tamed Aggression?') vs Caudate Motor-Steering Diagram
props.period_detail: separates 1965 newspaper mythology from basal-ganglia motor physiology

actions.verb_sequence: overlays the curved lateral turning arrow onto the caudate motor circuit

reactions.reaction: realize steering a muscle turn is NOT erasing anger

scenes.recognition_hook: The newspaper saw 'magical mind control' — frame-by-frame neuroanatomy saw a forced left turn in the caudate nucleus!

scenes.title: Modern Deep Brain Stimulation: Putting the Button in the Patient's Hand

layout.description: Warm sunlit clinic table where an older Parkinson's patient holds their own sleek white patient programmer beside a full clear glass of water.

positions.where: tapping 'ON' on their own personal DBS controller — hand steadying instantly to lift the water glass without spilling a drop!
smiling beside them with informed-consent care plan

props.name: patient-held DBS remote & steady water glass
props.period_detail: ethical triumph of wireless basal-ganglia stimulation under patient agency

actions.verb_sequence: taps personal DBS remote -> tremor ceases -> lifts water glass smoothly to lips

scenes.wardrobe: Modern cardigan and white physician coat.
scenes.recognition_hook: Sixty years after Córdoba, basal-ganglia pulses steady 250,000 trembling hands — with the remote control strictly in the patient's own palm.

scenes.title: Applying the Córdoba Skeptic's Filter to Modern Neurotech Hype

layout.description: Sunlit studio desk with a crisp 3-question checklist next to a wireless BCI headset.

positions.where: checking '1. Which exact brain region? 2. Motor/sensory signal or thought? 3. Who holds consent?'

actions.verb_sequence: checks off anatomical target and patient consent guardrails

scenes.recognition_hook: Whenever a viral headline shouts 'Brain Chip Controls Minds!', ask the Córdoba question: did it change a thought, or steer a motor loop?
